findings.title: [P1] Define or implement `renderError` before calling it
findings.body: `SearchController` (src/search.ts:19-30) declares no `renderError` method, extends no base class, and a repository-wide search finds the only occurrence of `renderError` is the new call site itself (src/search.ts:27). At runtime, the first time `this.api.search` rejects, the catch block throws `TypeError: this.renderError is not a function`, replacing the original error — the PR's entire new behavior never executes and the real error is masked. TypeScript also reports TS2339 (`Property 'renderError' does not exist`) at this new line. Unlike the pre-existing references (`api`, `render`, `active`), this method is newly invented by the diff with no definition or provider anywhere.

findings.title: [P2] Ignore failures from superseded searches before rendering an error
findings.body: Every `search()` call aborts the previous `this.active` controller (src/search.ts:21). With fetch-like `api.search` semantics, aborting an in-flight request rejects it with an `AbortError`, so the new unconditional catch renders a user-facing error during a perfectly normal search-replacement flow (type-ahead, rapid re-queries). A late-rejecting older request can also paint a stale error over the newer query's result. Capture the request's controller (e.g. `const { signal } = this.active`) inside the try and skip `renderError` when the failure is an abort or the controller is no longer `this.active`.

findings.title: [P3] Raw error objects are passed to the error renderer
findings.body: When `renderError` is implemented, it will receive raw exception objects that may embed internal URLs, backend messages, request metadata, or stack traces; displaying or serializing them can leak internals. Map exceptions to a safe public message and route detailed diagnostics to a logging sink instead. Worth settling now, while the error-rendering contract introduced by this diff is being defined.

findings.title: [P3] Add coverage for the new error path
findings.body: The change introduces materially different handling for rejected API requests (rendered error vs. propagated rejection), yet no tests exercise it — the repository currently has no test harness at all. At minimum, cover: API rejection renders an error, and a superseded/aborted request does not.
